blocks.x: Long-running workflows with durable state, recovery by design and escalation choreography: orchestration that survives partial failure, duplicate triggers and the Tuesday afternoon when the third-party API goes down mid-process.
Workflows fail on week three, not in the demo

A workflow that spans days — onboarding, claims, order-to-cash exceptions — is not a function call; it is a state machine that must survive restarts, token expiries, downstream outages and people going on holiday. The engineering is durable execution: every step idempotent, every state persisted, every failure path drawn before the happy path is celebrated.

Autonomy enters in the recovery: the orchestrator retries with backoff, reroutes around degraded systems, escalates when the policy says so, and never loses a unit of work. The audit is the twin: every state transition lands in a trail that answers 'what happened to case 40217' in one query.
The sections below cover the failure modes that produce zombie work, the architecture that makes state durable, and the console that shows recovery behavior under injected failure.
Four failure modes that turn orchestration into case debt
Every one of these leaves work stranded rather than failed — which is why they hide until SLA breaches surface them, and why each countermeasure is a structural property of the runtime.

headers: What it looks like in production
rows: Zombie work
Cases stuck mid-flight after a deploy; nobody owns them
Durable state store with age alarms and ownership routing per state
Duplicate side effects
Retry fires the payment twice; reconciliation finds it weeks later
Idempotency keys on every side effect; exactly-once ledger for money paths
Escalation black holes
Escalations route to a queue nobody reads
Escalation SLAs with paging; escalation success measured like conversion
Flow drift
The drawn process diverges from the running one after months of patches
Declarative workflow definitions in version control; drift diff in CI

blocks.x: Reference architecture — durable state and choreographed escalation

The design centers on three guarantees: state survives process restarts, side effects are idempotent under duplicate triggers, and escalation follows a choreography with timers — so nothing waits forever and nothing fires twice.

blocks.note: Compensation logic is a first-class artifact: every non-idempotent step has a defined undo, tested in the chaos drills, not improvised during an incident.

On-time completion, zombie count, duplicate side effects and escalation success — the four numbers that tell you whether the runtime is managing work or generating case debt.

blocks.title: Autonomous workflow orchestration — instance-health console

widgets.title: In-flight instances by age band — is the process draining or damming?
widgets.note: The >24 h band is the one to watch: a draining process empties it daily; a damming process lets it grow while the <1 h band looks healthy. Hover to read exact counts.

widgets.title: Elasticity what-if — burst intake vs worker fleet
widgets.note: Burst intake is the truth-teller for elastic design: the drain-time curve against pods shows where autoscaling stops helping because the downstream dependency, not the fleet, is the constraint.

widgets.title: Payment-onboarding saga — click any step for its compensation contract

nodes.label: KYC intake
nodes.detail: Typed document set with schema validation; a malformed intake never enters the saga — it returns to the submitter with reasons.

nodes.label: Sanctions screening
nodes.detail: Calls the screening provider with idempotency key; pended outcomes park on a timer with a 24 h re-screen policy.

nodes.label: Risk score
nodes.detail: Model step — pinned model version recorded per instance so a post-incident review knows exactly which score decided.

nodes.label: Account provisioning
nodes.detail: The first uncompensatable-by-default step: compensation is a documented account-closure flow with its own SLA, not a rollback.

nodes.label: Card issuance
nodes.detail: Compensable — cancellation API; the saga holds the cancellation token for the retention window.

nodes.label: Initial funding
nodes.detail: Ledger write with two-phase commit into the core-banking adapter; reconciliation job is the last line of defence.

nodes.label: Customer comms
nodes.detail: Idempotent notification with template pinning; retries respect quiet-hours policy.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read each compensation contract. The saga is only as strong as its weakest undo — we test that weakness deliberately.
